facts.claim: In Schroeder and Gibson’s 2007 study of disks in large real systems, 2–4% of disks needing replacement each year was common, and some systems reached 13%.

US-CERT’s Data Backup Options (Ruggiero and Heckathorn, 2012) gives the 3-2-1 rule: keep 3 copies of any important file, 1 primary and 2 backups; on 2 different kinds of storage; and store 1 copy offsite.
CISA’s #StopRansomware Guide (2023) says many ransomware variants try to find and delete or encrypt accessible backups, and asks for offline, encrypted backups of critical data.
In Sophos’s State of Ransomware 2024 survey of organisations hit in the year before, 94% said attackers tried to compromise their backups, and 57% of those attempts succeeded.
NIST SP 800-34 defines the recovery point objective as the point in time to which data must be recovered after an outage.
NIST SP 800-34 defines the recovery time objective as how long a system can be in recovery before it harms the organisation’s mission.
PostgreSQL 17’s manual says restoring an incremental backup needs the incremental itself and every earlier backup it depends on.
GitLab’s 2017 outage post-mortem says its nightly database dumps had been failing unnoticed and no one owned testing the restore; it lost about 6 hours of data.
NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (2010) says the shorter the recovery time you ask for, the more recovery costs, so the target is set by weighing the cost of being down against the cost of recovering.
